To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Subtilase Cytotoxic (SubAB), a virulence factor of Shiga-toxin producing E. coli, suppresses LPS-induced NO generation in macrophages by inhibition of NF-kB activation, which leads to increased bacterial survival.

Subtilase cytotoxic (SubAB) toxin, produced by certain Shiga-toxicien Escherichia (STEC) strains, inhibits LPS-induced iNOs expression through the inhibition of the nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) activation.
Subtilase Cytotoxic (SubAB) inhibits NF-κB-dependent nitric oxide (iNOS expression) production, which is critical for killing Escherichia (E.) coli in macrophages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms by which a bacterial toxin suppresses host innate immunity, leading to bacterial survival in the host.
the mechanism by which the Shiga-toxins produced by STEC inhibit the innate immune response of macrophages and how this contributes to the pathogenesis of STEC infection.
the role of SubAB in the inhibition of LPS-induced NO generation through the inhibition of NF-κ B activation and the effect of SubAB on E. coli survival.

SubAB suppresses LPS-induced NO synthesis through inhibition of NF-κb activation, and this effect contributes to E. coli intracellular survival in macrophage.

SubAB suppresses the innate immune response by inhibition of NF-κβ activation and NO production, thereby contributing to the pathogenesis of STEC.
